paragraphs: Chapter 1034
Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (1)
The Kinzelo Headquarters, with all its underground storage facilities open, was preparing to move once again.
While the members were tirelessly moving their belongings, as always, Bubare and Ainas were the only ones sitting in the corner of the central hall, giggling.
“Sigh…”
Bishkel looked down at the strands of hair in his hand with a haggard face. They had just fallen out carelessly when he brushed his forehead, and the amount was alarmingly high.
Now, he envied Bubare and Ainas. That they could be so blissfully happy and carefree when the Vamel Alliance had just risen as the strongest force and was advising surrender.
‘What could possibly be in their heads? Brains, or just fluffy dough? Probably the latter.’
Imagining the dough, Bishkel unknowingly let out a low laugh. Seeing him laugh vacantly, the officers nearby felt pity for him.
Everyone pitied their own plight. It sounded nice to say they were moving, but in reality, Kinzelo was preparing to flee and hide.
“Bishkel, pull yourself together.”
“Ah, I apologize for showing an unseemly side, Pirobs.”
“It’s okay. I’m worried too. Where in the world are we supposed to go…?”
They were packing, but in truth, there was nowhere left to hide in the Human World.
With airships becoming commonplace, virtually no part of the surface was hidden anymore, and the underworld had recently come to an end with the defeat of the Demon Realm.
Moreover, the Vamel Alliance had a record magician. Whether on the surface or underground, if Valeria decided to track them, they were bound to be caught.
Today is May 26, 1804, the day after the 'Lafrarosa Speech' ended. Now, Kinzelo only had six days left. Whether to surrender, fight, or flee, a decision had to be made within that time.
Naturally, this was not the future Kinzelo had envisioned.
When they first decided to induce the battle between the Vamel Alliance and the Red Plutonian, they had hoped to buy a lot of time.
However, the battle was full of unexpected variables, and during it, the summoning of the Demon Trio seemed to give Kinzelo some advantage, but the fight ended in less than a month.
There was no beautiful future of benefiting from the conflict between others. Only the worst outcome of Lafrarosa's liberation remained.
[Hey, why so gloomy? We can always go to the abyss, right?]
The Demon Trio approached the two men.
Since the liberation of Lafrarosa, they had become able to leave the Mitra Desert. However, they lost the ability to ignore physical attacks.
The Demon Trio regaining strength beyond their prime was a consolation for Kinzelo, but still incomparable to the Vamel Alliance, which had acquired Lafrarosa.
“We can only stay in the abyss if we're dead, right, Sribi? And we need the witch's permission too…”

[That's right, Pirobs. Permission is needed. That's why the witch called Orgal this time, right? But it's wrong that only the dead can live there. With the witch's permission, even the living can stay.]
Currently, Orgal was in the abyss, having been summoned by the witch Heluram. There was something 'to receive and to give,' as the witch had messaged.
That was also why Kinzelo was just packing without a destination. The decision-maker, Orgal, was absent.
[Masalrun thinks the witch doesn't want Orgal to die. Thus, we might survive under the witch's protection, even if we don't surrender to the Vamel Alliance.]
“Oh, then the members too.”
[But you are not special to the witch. She might save Orgal and not care about what happens to you.]
Hearing this, Pirobs sighed, and Bishkel clenched his teeth. Sribi agreed, thinking it made sense.
“Ever since we devoted ourselves to Kinzelo for a great cause, we have never expected help from the witch. As always, we will find a way this time too. With our own strength.”
“Oh, big brother, you’re so cool!”
It was Margiella. She looked emaciated from her recent rampages, but her eyes sparkled with mischief as usual.
“Margiella. Are you alright?”
“Of course, big brother. It’s a bit sad that I can’t help with the move because of my condition.”
Bishkel clenched his teeth, unable to suppress his sorrow. He longed to see his sister healthy just once, a wish that haunted him like a nightmare.
But Margiella herself wasn't sad or depressed at all. She smiled and looked around at Bishkel and Pirobs.
“Don't worry too much, Commander Pirobs. When the leader returns, a decision will be made. Maybe, we won't need to hide anymore?”
“Are you suggesting that our leader might choose to surrender to the Vamel Alliance?”
“Eh, I doubt it. Although there are some aspects of Jin’s goals that align with our great mission, they are ultimately not the same. I don’t think our leader would choose to fade away in defeat.”
[It almost sounds like you would consider surrendering.]
“That’s right, Sribi!”
Sribi chuckled at Margiella's bright response.

[Indeed, unless the witch gives Orgal something significant, we have no other options. Everyone here is living on borrowed time. We could just return to the abyss, but as Masalrun said, you are just like air to the witch, or even less.]
“Should we form an alliance with Zipfel again, like in the past...?”
Bubare's mutter made the members shake their heads. Now that Zipfel's power of the Origin Stone had grown too vast, allying with them meant being a disposable pawn or a sacrificial lamb to buy time.

“But let’s not live in worry, everyone! My power is gradually awakening, and I think I can control it. I don’t want to fight Jin with this power, but if they push us to the edge, we might have no choice.”
“...Really, Margiella? Can you control it?”
“Maybe, Commander Pirobs. Of course, it will take more time than the six days Jin gave us. And fortunately, there seem to be people who can buy us that time.”
“People who can buy us time?”
The members’ attention focused on Margiella.
“Yes, many. There are those who can’t be forgiven and those like us who won’t seek forgiveness.”
Zipfel, Ganesto, and the Sun God Religion.
Margiella was particularly interested in the Sun God Religion. Recently, the sense of the ‘inherent’ being within her had awakened, letting her feel what they were up to.

“The Sun God Religion. If I’m right… they will soon make a foolish choice. A meaningless and stupid one. So let's pack our belongings well and calmly wait for the leader. I hope the leader brings some good news.”
Deep in the Black Sea, in the realm of the Five Kings.
A crow, out of place in the Black Sea, was crossing the dark and murky sky. The sky was filled with sharp cracks, as if made of broken glass, ready to collapse at any moment.
‘My brothers…’
The crow’s name was Nirgand.
One of the only two remaining Kings of the Black Sea, the fourth fragment of the Origin Stone. He was feeling the pain of his previously deceased brothers, Gliek, Kial, and Su.
And he was running away.
‘Chiron Runcandel. How did he transcend all those fates? His power should have been exhausted, but why has he become even stronger? Has he really achieved eternal transcendence…?’

Just as Su despaired in front of Chiron's sword, Nirgand couldn’t comprehend him either. His dream of uniting with his brothers through Chiron vanished like a bubble, leaving only the threat of extinction.
The Five Kings of the Black Sea couldn’t unite without Chiron's power. Even if ‘Morganil,’ the strongest fragment, was somewhere in this realm, they couldn’t help each other.
[Aaagh…]
Suddenly, Nirgand’s wing buckled.
It was because of a wound inflicted by Chiron's sword ten days ago. In the past ten days, Nirgand had encountered Chiron three times and fled each time.
Being caught was only a matter of time. With each encounter, his wounds increased, and if it continued, he would perish within days.
Now, he couldn’t even escape the realm of the Five Kings. He couldn’t buy enough time to recover and remove the constraints.

Although Chiron should be at least a million steps away, his blade felt coldly flickering behind him. Chiron, having transcended Genesis, was an invincible being even to Nirgand, as Su had so easily succumbed to him.
‘Morganil, brother. Do you know that Chiron has become a disaster? Are you moving because of it, or are you running away miserably like me? Hiding.’
Just as he was about to lift his heavy body and spread his wings again.
Nirgand suddenly realized that Chiron was approaching. A vast force was pouring in through the darkness ahead.
There was no hope against Chiron. But even if Chiron had transcended Genesis, he couldn’t suddenly teleport within the realm of the Five Kings.
Nirgand calmly read the energy again.
‘It’s not Chiron. Just another mortal who has reached Genesis.’
After pondering for a few seconds, Nirgand started to flap his wings forward. As he drew closer, a white light flickered, something never seen among the Five Kings of the Black Sea.
It was a warm energy that Nirgand had never felt before. Staring quietly at the light, he felt inexplicably at ease, as if he had encountered the light of his homeland after a long time.
From within the light, two people emerged. The high priest Luke of the Sun God Religion and the priestess Sanna.
“Hello, King Nirgand of the Black Sea. It's sudden, but I greet you. I am Sanna, the priestess of the Sun God Religion.”
Sanna bowed her head and spoke first. Luke, standing beside her, showed no signs of the wounds he had received from Jin.
“And this is our High Priest Luke.”
[...The Sun God Religion?]
“We seem to be in a similar situation. How about studying the Sun God together? It will be helpful for both us and for you, Nirgand.”
